label: Unity carriage map: simplicity locates root exclusions; carriage as such needs a bridge
meaning: Certificate for #2145 lane U. Clause 1: on the reading on which every real constituent of a root realizes a determination, simplicity is idle. Clause 2: a classical source meets every unity premise, both transfers, carriage in both senses, the necessity direction, own-nature exclusion and E (positive witness). Clause 3: a simple source that lacks noesis by a clause of its one nature meets every unity premise, TRANSFER_2 and carriage in the root, while TRANSFER_1, own-nature carriage as such, LE, the sense bridge, E and the purity of requirements in the root fail: unity gives its lack a positive ground in the root, its one nature, and the step to carriage as such is the sense bridge, which fails in that row. Clause 4: on the open family with the necessity direction no requirement relation lets that source meet own-nature carriage as such, and its being, which the thinking effect shares, cannot require the lack of noesis as such. Clauses 5 to 8 drop simplicity, SEAT, REAL and ESSE in turn, with the other unity premises and TRANSFER_1 holding and own-nature carriage failing. Clause 9: the unity package with own-nature carriage holds while the necessity direction and E fail, so the unity argument has no bearing on the necessity direction. Clause 10: with a fine-grained 'this nature' determination that requires as such the lack of noesis, the unity premises, TRANSFER_1, own-nature carriage, the sense bridge, the necessity direction and E hold, and the source pays either the purity of requirements (the nature determination pure: the Plotinian line) or strict purity at roots (the nature determination impure). Clause 11: on lane E's selection carrier the classical source, with a selection read as a real determination that varies across worlds, meets the unity premises, TRANSFER_1, own-nature carriage, the necessity direction, own-nature exclusion and E while N fails; whether one world-invariant constituent can realize different selections at different worlds is not encoded. Clause 12: with clause 3, the simple source that lacks noesis meets every premise of everyPureFromCarriageIn except the purity of requirements in the root, and lacks a pure determination; the classical source meets them all. Establishes no premise.
